Title: Diagnosis of test `testContainsAnyStringWithSupplementaryChars`

Details:
1. The test `testContainsAnyStringWithSupplementaryChars` calls `StringUtils.containsAny` with two arguments named `CharU20000` and `CharU20001`. These are presumably supplementary Unicode character strings (characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane).
2. The `StringUtils.containsAny(CharSequence, String)` method converts the `String` argument to a `char[]` and delegates to `StringUtils.containsAny(CharSequence, char[])`.
3. The `StringUtils.containsAny(CharSequence, char[])` method checks for the presence of any character from the `searchChars` array in the character sequence `cs` by iterating over the `cs` characters and comparing each to the `searchChars` elements using `char` equality.
4. The failure appears because the method only iterates over the `char` units of the `CharSequence`, which are UTF-16 code units. Supplementary characters are represented by surrogate pairs (two `char`s) in UTF-16.
5. As a result, the method does not properly handle supplementary characters composed of two `char`s. It treats them as two separate `char` values instead of a single code point, leading to incorrect matching behavior.
6. Hence, the method fails to correctly determine whether supplementary characters appear in the search input, causing the test to fail.

This diagnosis is consistent with the test asserting that the result of checking two different supplementary character strings for containment returns `false`, but the internal method does not correctly compare supplementary characters as whole code points.

The root cause is the lack of support for supplementary Unicode characters in the `containsAny` methods, which only perform `char`-level comparisons.

Next, I will suggest which methods would be the best locations to fix this bug.
org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.containsAny(java.lang.CharSequence, char[])
org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.containsAny(java.lang.CharSequence, java.lang.String)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
